_doc: PHASE 1 RESULTS -- pass-gate XNOR2/MUX2 on a QAL rail. Pre-registration PRE_REGISTERED.json sha256 6b6d6663df54b544bcb09122c05124ff0919fcd4b7b9caf87c064b94aaeb75fd, written 2026-09-29 11:46:11 -0700 when qal/pgcell/ held one 0-byte file. MEASURED unless a row says DERIVED or ASSUMED. Every device number is a LOWER BOUND: sg13lv_compat.sp drops instance ad/as/pd/ps so the PSP103 model-card junction defaults apply and no layout parasitics are present.

anchor.C_chain_control: the CTL chain (4 inverter banks, tank-fed) reproduces the committed banktank headline: rails 0.7544/0.6767/0.7312/0.7201 V, separations 706.56/612.38/619.51/671.43 mV, IZ -0.0076/-0.0012/-0.0031/-0.0030 uA -- all digit-identical to qal/banktank/README.md.

protocol_amendments_forced_by_measuremen.P1_pass_pMOS_well_is_a_FREE_VARIABLE_not: NOT in the pre-registration; forced by measurement before any verdict. The naive port of the campaign's static-cell convention ties the pass pMOS n-well to the BANK RAIL. On a rail that ramps from 0 a data input already at the predecessor's HIGH then sits ~0.7 V above its own well for the whole ramp and FORWARD-BIASES the p+/n-well junction. MEASURED on the failing vector (G_diag.cir, TG-XNOR2 A=1 B=0): with the well on the rail the cell's own inverter output ab is held at 0.598 V at t=0 when it should be 0 V, and the output bootstraps to 0.989 V (ABOVE the 0.714 V rail) at the step. With the well on the +1.5 V supply the architecture already carries, ab reads 0.045 V. Both ties are therefore built and reported everywhere; neither is assumed.
protocol_amendments_forced_by_measuremen.P2_probe_window: bt.deck sizes a ZCS probe window from the committed INVERTER bank's zero (2.6*TZ_ANCH). A pass-gate bank's RETURN half-cycle is longer -- MEASURED on ALLTG ret1, peak return current only -40.87 uA against +874 uA on the rise, peaking at 1111.5 ps and still -7.27 uA at the 1170.3 ps window end -- so zero_after_peak CORRECTLY reported NO ZERO. Fixed by lengthening the RETURN probe window 3x (PROBE_RET_MULT). Nothing about the measured circuit changed; the rise windows and every other committed constant are untouched.
protocol_amendments_forced_by_measuremen.P3_timestep: The cell/raildraw decks run at .tran 0.02p/0.05p (4x FINER than the committed 0.05p/0.2p). The LEVEL deck and the D2 supplement run at the committed 0.05p/0.2p. Both resolutions reproduce the committed anchors (anchor B at 0.02p/0.05p, rel <= 3.7e-6; the per-deck 1.2 V CMOS instrument check reads 57.1422-57.1424 ps at both against the committed 57.143).
protocol_amendments_forced_by_measuremen.P4_deck_S_split: The full static-control deck (56 cases x 4 rails) exceeded the 1500 s timeout; it was re-run as S1 at the reference rail only (14 cases, 174 s). The rail sweep of the static controls is therefore NOT measured in this phase and is not claimed. Decks R1/R2 (the TG rail sweep) were likewise not run -- the rail grid 0.68/0.7544/1.26 V is UNMEASURED and no verdict rests on it.
protocol_amendments_forced_by_measuremen.P5_vae_cache_key_includes_W: MEASURED TRAP worth recording for the campaign: the PyMS vae .so cache key folds the DEVICE PARAMETERS and W is one of them (vae_PSP103VA_<hash>.so.params carries W=7.4e-07, W=1.12e-06, ...). One GiNaC C++ compile PER WIDTH PER TYPE, ~3-5 min each on a loaded box, and a deck that introduces a new width stalls before its first timestep. A width sweep is therefore expensive in WALL TIME, not in simulation. warm.py pre-builds each missing width in its own tiny deck so the builds run in parallel (distinct keys; the campaign's 'one at a time' rule is about the SAME key).

a_rail_draw.predicted: TG-PROPER rail charge under 5% of the whole cell; whole cell within 2x of the static sg13g2_xnor2_1; TG-MUX2 the cheapest of the three.
a_rail_draw.verdict: SPLIT. CONFIRMED that the gates themselves draw nothing -- and more strongly than predicted: with the well off the rail a transmission gate draws EXACTLY 0.0000 fC / 0.0000 fJ from the bank supply. REFUTED as written for the rail-well tie: TG-PROPER there draws 3.77 fC / 1.47 fJ, which is 28% of the whole TG-XNOR2 cell and 122% of a whole static inverter, not <5%. The entire TG-proper draw IS the n-well. Whole-cell-within-2x CONFIRMED (13.47 vs 8.83 fC = 1.53x).

b_level_loss.predicted: steady-state loss under 5 mV both polarities through one cell; chained loss SUB-ADDITIVE and dominated by the first stage.
b_level_loss.verdict: SPLIT. Single-cell CONFIRMED and then some on the transparent path (|loss| <= 0.23 mV at the checkpoint, 0.000 mV at the long tail, both polarities, either well). Chained SUB-ADDITIVITY REFUTED: measured loss GROWS with depth in every pass-gate cascade (TGMUX rail-well LOW, ideal source: 527.0 / 672.0 / 721.2 / 738.5 mV at depths 1-4). Mechanism measured, not assumed: a transmission gate is BIDIRECTIONAL, so every downstream stage's off-path injection sums and has to be sunk backwards through the whole series chain into the single driver.

c_non_restoring_compound.predicted: the ALTERNATING chain HOLDS -- separation above 6.44 mV with the correct sign at every depth, lower than the all-inverter control but still >= 50x the floor; and the failure mode, if any, would be a reduction SPECIFICALLY AT THE TG DEPTHS rather than a monotone fade.
c_non_restoring_compound.verdict: REFUTED on the headline. The alternating chain does not hold: it loses the VALUE by bank 3 in both well ties, and the fixed-well arrangement ends at 5.49 mV = 0.85x the floor. The named failure mode is CONFIRMED for the fixed well (459.0 inv -> 55.4 tg -> 145.0 inv -> 5.49 tg: the inverter stage DOES restore, 2.6x, but not enough) and REFUTED for the rail well, which fades monotonically (416.7 / 186.2 / 106.0 / 24.6 mV). So alternating restores PARTIALLY; the pass-gate stages compound faster than one inverter stage repairs.
